x: MIDH is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme running since 2014-15. 2005-06 is the launch year of the National Horticulture Mission, which MIDH later subsumed.
Banana is India's top fruit by production, ahead of mango, apple and grapes.
Andhra Pradesh is 4th in coconut production. It is 1st in oil palm (2.27 lakh ha), so do not confuse the two rankings.
Emircha is AP's digital horticulture programme run with Digital Green. ICAR-CIFRI, MPEDA and NFDB are fisheries bodies.
India is the largest producer of turmeric, and the National Turmeric Board is at Nizamabad. In silk India is only 2nd, so 'Silk' is the trap.
The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) came in 2020. Rashtriya Gokul Mission and the National Livestock Mission are the 2014 schemes.
PMMSY, the flagship Blue Revolution scheme, was launched in 2020 with ₹20,050 crore. It ran from FY 2020-21 to 2024-25 and was extended to 2025-26.
Andhra Pradesh, India's largest aquaculture and farmed-shrimp (mostly Vannamei) producer, accounts for about 29-30% of the country's fish output.
The Chittoor fodder crisis, with a 62% rainfall deficit in June-July 2026, came with El Niño conditions, which weaken the monsoon. La Niña usually brings more rain.
Andhra Pradesh leads India in fruit production; it also leads in shrimp, oil palm and eggs. Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka are not first in fruit.
The APPSC-GS 2025 key used 'around 23%' as the share of processed food exports for 2024-25, so pick the option offered. 11.86% is a different figure: agri exports' share of merchandise exports.
There were only 5 CPSEs when the First Plan began. The number rose to 244 by 1990 and is now over 250.

The Department of Public Enterprises is now under the Ministry of Finance. Older notes placed it under the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises, so 'Heavy Industries' is the stale answer.
The Navratna scheme began in 1997 with nine PSUs. 14 and 26 are the Maharatna and Navratna counts as on 1 April 2025.
In the old eight-core series, fertilisers had the lowest weight (2.63%). They are still the lowest in the new 2022-23 series (2.73%).
SSI reservation began in 1967 with 47 items. It peaked at about 873 items in 1984, and the last 20 items were dereserved in 2015.
The Planning Commission set up the Karve Committee in 1955 on village and small industries for the Second Plan. Some notes print '1995', which is an OCR error.
ECLGS was the Covid-era emergency credit-guarantee line for MSMEs (2020); ECLGS 5.0 followed in May 2026. The other options describe MSME Samadhaan (2017), SFCs (SFC Act 1951) and TReDS.
Udyam Registration, a free and paperless self-declaration portal, started in 2020; registrations are counted from 1 July 2020.
In February 2026 the RBI said MSE loans up to ₹20 lakh need no collateral; banks may extend this to ₹25 lakh.
Budget 2026-27 gave the Self-Reliant India Fund a ₹2,000 crore top-up. ₹10,000 crore is the separate SME Growth Fund.
Budget 2026-27 announced a ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund to build 'Champion MSMEs'. ₹2,000 crore is the separate top-up to the Self-Reliant India Fund.
The mandatory share was raised from 20% to 25% in 2018. 2012 is the year of the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order itself.

AP MSME & Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 covers 2024-29 and was issued through G.O.Ms.No.69 dated 26 October 2024. 2019 is the year of YSR Navodayam, and 2026 brought a revamped MSME Policy for women-led units, not a 2026-31 policy.
